_comment: Item 58 evidence library (gw 2.0/EVIDENCE_LIBRARY.md E1-E10). Changed only with a release. E6: every entry is drafted against its paper and shows in the app only once Rob has accepted it (status 'accepted' with accepted_on). 'checked_against' says what of the paper was read for the draft; an entry checked only against its abstract should be read against the full paper before it is accepted.

entries.finding: Across 138 experiments, helping people check their progress toward a goal more often made them more likely to reach it. The effect was larger when the progress was written down or reported.
entries.limits: Most of the studies were about health goals such as exercise, diet and weight, not money. It is an average across studies; it does not say how often any one person should check.

source.title: Does monitoring goal progress promote goal attainment? A meta-analysis of the experimental evidence

entries.offer: Want a weekly reminder to look at your goals?
entries.checked_against: abstract and the accepted manuscript's record (White Rose eprints 91437)

entries.finding: Investors in Sweden and the United States looked at their accounts more often when markets were rising than when markets were flat or falling.
entries.limits: It studied investors and their portfolios, not household budgets. It describes a pattern across many people and says nothing about why any one person looks or does not.

source.title: The ostrich effect: Selective attention to information

entries.offer: Want a weekly reminder that comes whatever the week looked like?

entries.finding: Logins to online retirement accounts fell by about 9.5% after the market fell, and were lower when market volatility was high.
entries.limits: Retirement-plan investors at one provider. How much attention people paid also varied with age, gender and wealth.
entries.offer: Want a weekly reminder that comes whatever the week looked like?

entries.finding: At one company, employees who agreed in advance to send part of each future raise to retirement saving went from saving 3.5% of pay to 13.6% by their fourth raise.
entries.limits: One employer's plan, and the workers who chose to join it. A later U.S. Department of Labor review rated the causal evidence low. It is about raises and retirement plans.

source.title: Save More Tomorrow: Using behavioral economics to increase employee saving

entries.offer: Want to decide now how much of your next raise goes to a goal?
entries.checked_against: working-paper abstract and the Department of Labor CLEAR summary; the published abstract was not read

entries.finding: When one company began enrolling new employees in its retirement plan automatically, far more took part, and many kept the plan's default contribution rate and fund.
entries.limits: One large U.S. company. Many people stayed at the default even where it was not the rate they would have chosen, so a default carries weight either way.

source.title: The power of suggestion: Inertia in 401(k) participation and savings behavior

entries.offer: Want to set one monthly amount for this goal and leave it in place?

entries.finding: Among about 6,000 people in a debt settlement program, closing individual debt accounts went with finishing the program, whatever the dollar size of the accounts closed.
entries.limits: People in a debt settlement program. It shows a link, not that closing the smallest debt first causes success, and paying the highest rate first still costs less interest.

source.title: Can small victories help win the war? Evidence from consumer debt management

entries.offer: Want to see the plan that closes a debt soonest beside the one that costs the least interest?
entries.checked_against: Kellogg School research and news pages; the abstract itself was not read

entries.finding: People who meant to pay only part of a credit card bill chose to repay less when the bill showed the minimum payment.
entries.limits: A UK survey and hypothetical bills. People who pay the whole balance each month were not affected.

source.title: The cost of anchoring on credit-card minimum repayments

entries.offer: Want to set your own monthly payment for each card, apart from the minimum?
entries.checked_against: abstract opening (Warwick repository) and the university's press release

entries.finding: In field experiments at three banks, new savings-account holders who were sent reminders were more likely to reach their savings goal, most of all when the reminder named the goal.
entries.limits: New account holders at banks in lower-income countries, with text reminders from the bank. Framing a reminder as a gain or a loss made no clear difference.

source.title: Getting to the top of mind: How reminders increase saving

entries.offer: Want a reminder that names this goal?
entries.checked_against: working-paper abstracts (NBER w16205 and the 2014 draft); the published abstract was not read

entries.finding: In a randomized trial at a bank in the Philippines, clients offered a savings account that held their money until a date or amount they chose had average balances 81 percentage points higher after a year than a comparison group.
entries.limits: Clients of one Philippine bank; about 28% of those offered the account opened one. Money held until a date is harder to reach in an emergency.

source.title: Tying Odysseus to the mast: Evidence from a commitment savings product in the Philippines

entries.offer: Want to give this goal a date and an amount to hold to?
entries.checked_against: abstract and the Yale ISPS record

entries.finding: Among low-income households in disadvantaged neighborhoods, those that set money aside for emergencies reported somewhat less hardship three years later, such as going without enough food or losing phone service.
entries.limits: Low-income households in particular neighborhoods, not a national sample. It shows a link, and the difference was modest; it does not show that saving caused the difference.

source.title: Emergency saving and household hardship
source.journal: Journal of Family and Economic Issues 37(1), 1-17

entries.offer: Want to start a small fund for emergencies?
entries.checked_against: abstract (IDEAS/RePEc record); the full text is paywalled and was not read
